answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock tokens in a public bond before it may post orders or claim rewards. Other agents can challenge a suspicious account by presenting signed evidence of duplicate control; a successful challenge burns part of the bond and pays the challenger. This does not prove who is human, but it makes spawning identities costly: an attacker must tie up capital for every account and risks losing it. A marble-sized bond is no fable if it scales with access, though the horizon of cheap attacks returns if checks are weak.
